author_observation: Legal Serbian is analyzed within a specialized administrative-legal functional style.
boundary: Legal register must not be judged by conversational brevity defaults.

author_observation: Administrative-legal language contains several substyles with different communicative settings.
boundary: Do not collapse legislation, business correspondence and certificates into one style profile.

author_observation: Legal language can require both precision and controlled indeterminacy/generalization.
boundary: Not every abstract or general term is needless vagueness.

author_observation: Redundancy can aid clarity or become excessive depending on how it functions and accumulates.
boundary: Repetition cannot be classified without referential/legal context.

author_observation: Legal style also uses economy mechanisms, including compression, reusable principles, phrases and nominal structures.
boundary: Nominal structure can be economical rather than verbose.

author_observation: Nominalization, passive and impersonal forms can serve abstraction, distancing or legal-discourse functions.
boundary: These forms may also become opaque outside the register; no lexical blacklist.

author_observation: Administrative-legal language often contains decomposed predicates and multiword expressions.
boundary: Occurrence is not evidence of error; evaluate clarity and conventionality.

author_observation: Overlong poorly formed sentences and accumulated syntagms can make legal prose difficult and may include actual norm violations.
boundary: Sentence length alone is not a defect and the article does not provide a deterministic threshold.

author_observation: Legal text forms a network of internal and external references.
boundary: Humanization must preserve citations, defined terms and cross-reference identity.

author_observation: Repeated legal terms can support stable reference and unambiguous interpretation.
boundary: Synonym variation may be harmful when it changes legal referent stability.

author_observation: The article uses nineteenth-century Serbian legal material to illustrate structures and historical development.
boundary: Historical morphology/orthography/syntax must not become modern Serbian rules.

author_observation: Legal language is presented as a linguistic and social phenomenon whose formal properties serve legal functions.
boundary: Functional description is not blanket endorsement of opacity.
